Name: Sales Call Research & Prep Brief
Scenario:
Your sales team doesn’t have a consistent research or preparation process before sales calls. Some reps skip the step entirely, while others do a minimal amount of research with mixed results. As the sales manager, you want to introduce a simple, repeatable, AI-powered workflow that makes sales prep fast, structured, and genuinely useful.
Create a templatized ChatGPT prompt flow that:
- Organizes all existing information the sales rep already has about the prospect
- Searches the web for additional relevant information (company news, market context, etc.)
- Generates a polished, strategic preparation brief the rep can skim before the call to maximize their chances of advancing the deal
Hints:
- Keep everything in a single ChatGPT thread so it can reuse context from each prompt.
- In Prompt 1, paste all your raw information at once instead of sending many small messages. The AI is good at organizing messy notes.
- Tell ChatGPT explicitly what role it’s playing (e.g. “You are my Sales Research & Preparation Partner”) to get more focused, relevant output.
- In Prompt 2, ask it to search the web, but be specific about what you care about (recent news, industry trends, funding, leadership changes, etc.).
- In Prompt 3, be very clear about the final deliverable: a brief you can skim in 2–3 minutes before the call, with specific sections (profile, objections, questions, call plan).
- Use phrases like “Think very long and hard” or “Be thorough and strategic in your reasoning” to push for deeper analysis, not just surface-level summaries.
- If the output feels off, don’t start over—just coach the AI inside the same thread (e.g., “Shorten this to one page,” “Make the objections section more specific to [industry]”).
Solution:
Prompt 1:
I am a sales person preparing for a sales call. Here’s all the information I have about my prospect:
- Their Name: [Full name]
- Organization: [Company name]
- LinkedIn text: [copy/paste text from profile]
- Transcript or notes from previous interactions: [paste here]
- My general notes or observations: [paste/type here]
Please synthesize the prospect’s information into a cohesive profile.

Prompt 2:
Their Website URL is: [URL]
Please search the web for recent and relevant information about this company and person. Look for:
- Company news, leadership announcements, or funding
- Industry trends affecting them
- Public partnerships or press coverage
- Any recent interviews or thought leadership content
Please add any new information to the prospect’s profile.

Prompt 3:
I am a part of the [Industry] industry, selling [Product].
The goal of my sales call is: [e.g., Schedule a demo / Close the deal / Gather discovery info / Build rapport / etc.]
Think very long and hard and create a Sales Call Preparation Document that includes:
1) The Prospect’s Profile: A concise summary of all the relevant information of my prospect from our chat history.
2) Objection Handling: A list of potential objections that my prospect may have that considers their unique background and their unique business/industry. Please include strategic objection handling responses.
3) Leading Questions: Generate a list of persuasive, leading questions designed to make someone recognize why they need my product or service.
Concept Names: The Parts of a Prompt, The Human-AI Sandwich, Upload Files, Lots of Context, Structure Context, Use AI to Pre-Process Context, Define Output Structure, Provide Examples, Break into Sub-Steps, Think Very Long and Hard, Use a Thinking Model, Parameterize Your Prompts, Organize a Prompt Library,  Require Checkable Sources, Remove Sensitive Data
Concept Descriptions:
The Parts of a Prompt - Define a clear objective, offer motivation, explain the audience, give instructions, specify the output, etc.
The Human-AI Sandwich - Let humans handle the first and last 10% (framing + final review) and AI handle the heavy middle.
Upload Files - Provide original files (PDFs, CSVs, docs) so the model can pull details from them when needed.
Lots of Context - Err on the side of giving more raw material (notes, transcripts, webpage dumps, and even pictures/screenshots) when unsure what’s needed.
Structure Context - Organize inputs into labeled sections like BACKGROUND, GOAL, CONSTRAINTS, EXAMPLES.
Use AI to Pre-Process Context - First ask the model to summarize or reorganize large, messy inputs into compact, structured notes.
Define Output Structure - Describe the exact fields and columns you want the model to return.
Provide Examples - Show a model answer and tell the AI to follow that style and structure. Note: Experiment with this, because the model can often copy the example too closely.
Break into Sub-Steps - Decompose big tasks into smaller steps (outline A & B → draft A → draft B).
Think Very Long and Hard - Add this for extra computation. Note: This only works on reasoning models.
Use a Thinking Model - Use a reasoning-focused model when accuracy and logical depth matter most.
Parameterize Your Prompts - Add variables like {{Audience}}, {{Tone}}, and {{Length}} so prompts can be reused easily.
Organize a Prompt Library - Maintain a catalog of your best prompts by use case and domain.
Require Checkable Sources - Ask the AI to provide verifiable sources for factual claims.  Note: make sure to check them, because sources can also be hallucinated.
Remove Sensitive Data - Avoid including personal, confidential, or regulated information unless you’re in a compliant setup.
